Technical Philosophy Better Buildings Partners often are faced with how to make decisions as to what retrofits to undertake to save energy. A key objective of this activity is to help participants improve their conceptual understanding of energy retrofits and to observe the sensitivities of different decision- making tradeoffs as they make the business case for saving energy. The activity has been designed without a specific problem statement, and as such there is no predetermined solution or “correct answer”. Participants begin the activity by determining and stating the goal(s) they want the sample building to meet. The challenge posed by the activity is then for participants to identify the best combination of retrofit measures to meet their goals. Retrofit measures have been grouped into the following categories for the activity: - Envelope - Lighting - Plug Loads - Ventilation - Domestic Hot Water - Heating/Cooling - Solar PV Each category includes a range of options that is representative of the current state of the market, including a “do nothing” option. The retrofit options are not presented with energy savings, but rather as additive components of the building’s energy use that are combined to build an alternate retrofit scenario that is compared to the baseline scenario to determine savings. Because of the interdependence of building components on overall energy use, individual measures are difficult to evaluate without knowing other details about the building. For example, replacing the heating system with a more efficient alternative saves energy on its own but those savings are amplified if the building envelope is also upgraded to reduce heat loss. Therefore, this activity has been designed to evaluate savings after all building systems have been considered. Figure 1 helps to visualize this, where each category of building energy consumption stacks to an overall energy use intensity (EUI).
